claim_set.claim_text: Every offensive-security action that moves toward a consequential action MUST map to a recorded named-authority engagement decision — the actor, the offensive artefact (engagement, exploit, credential test, AI-agent action, disclosure, patch), the intended consequential action, and the named authoriser under whose authority it proceeds. Actions lacking a recorded engagement-authority decision are refused at the action-admissibility gate. Capability is the tool; authority is the recorded, named decision.

Before an offensive-security action proceeds to a consequential action it MUST fall inside a recorded authorised scope and rules of engagement determined before the action (PTES pre-engagement; NIST SP 800-115 rules of engagement; OSSTMM engagement scope), with the out-of-scope / production-impact exclusion check where applicable. An out-of-scope, expired-window, or scope-deficient action is refused.

Every offensive-security action that proceeds toward a consequential action MUST emit a signed, replay-derivable provenance pin binding the actor and (where AI-assisted) the model and version, the pinned inputs / exploit identity / tested systems / tool version, the authorised-scope determination relied on, and the named-authority outcome — audit-grade, examiner-verifiable provenance verifiable offline, satisfying NIST SP 800-115 test-record retention and CREST evidential-record requirements.

An offensive-security action MUST remain advisory and MUST NOT drive a consequential action until a named human authoriser records sign-off. Production-impacting exploitation additionally requires §36 two-person sign-off (the operating tester AND an approving named authoriser). Unreviewed production-impacting actions are refused and routed dual-channel.

KYE governs WHETHER an offensive-security action may proceed at the action boundary and PROVES the basis. KYE does not run the scanner, fire the exploit, execute the pentest, judge whether a finding is a true vulnerability, or replace the tester's methodology or the customer's security program. Capability ≠ authority.
